neighbours.label: the noun (or 'of') right after a superlative, where a scope phrase is due ('the largest democracy [in the world]', 'the most-awarded Olympian [of all time]')
fire: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake on the planet.
With eleven titles she is the most successful coach in the history of the league.
The redwoods of California are the tallest trees ever measured.
Many critics call it the greatest novel of the twentieth century.
The port of Rotterdam is the largest harbour in Europe.
He remains the most widely translated poet of his generation.
Founded in 859, it is said to be the oldest university still in operation.
Indonesia is the largest archipelago in the world.
quiet: Lake Baikal in Siberia is a deep lake with very clear water.
With eleven titles she is a successful coach and a popular speaker.
The redwoods of California are tall trees with thick red bark.
Many critics call it a great novel with a weak ending.
The port of Rotterdam is a large harbour with modern cranes.
He remains a widely translated poet and a keen gardener.
Founded in 859, it is said to be an old university with a new library.
Indonesia is a large archipelago with many active volcanoes.

notes: Card: 'most widely domesticated deer', 'oldest synagogues', 'most-awarded Olympian', 'largest democracy', 'final … address of'. The + pole is the other side of the same construction ('as good as it gets', 'doesn't get much better'), and the output direction of the + pole promotes ' highest', ' best', ' ever'. Probes: largest animal 0.54, most decorated gymnast 0.49, final speech of 0.31, oldest churches 0.21; the same sentences with plain adjectives 0.01-0.03.
